cards.text: Josiah, king of Judah, just finished tearing down idol altars from the temple all the way to Bethel. Demolition crew, CLOCK OUT. Now he gives all the people a command straight out of the Book of the Covenant.

cards.question: Josiah tells all the people to keep a feast of the LORD their God, just as it's written in the Book of the Covenant. Which feast?

cards.text: Then the writer stops the story to tell you something about this Passover. And friend, it covers a LOT of history.

cards.question: How far back would you have to go to find a Passover like Josiah's?

cards.text: Since the JUDGES. Every king of Israel and Judah in between, and not one Passover like this. I spent years in a junk drawer and thought THAT was a long wait between batches.

cards.question: Josiah's Passover is kept to the LORD in Jerusalem, in the eighteenth year of his reign.

cards.text: And Josiah's not done cleaning house. There's still stuff hiding around the land, and he goes after it like I go after the last chocolate chip at the bottom of the bag.

cards.question: What else does Josiah clear out of Judah and Jerusalem?
Josiah clears all of it out to carry out the words of the ___ written in the book that Hilkiah the priest found in the house of the LORD.

cards.text: Then the writer steps back and sizes Josiah up against every king. Before him AND after him. Friend, that is a TOUGH room.

cards.question: Of all the kings before Josiah and after him, there was no king like Josiah.
Josiah turned to the LORD with all his heart, soul and strength, according to all the Law of ___.

cards.text: Josiah just got the best review of any king, before or after. Then the writer says, "Nevertheless," and friend, you know that word. It's your boss saying "Great quarter" and then taking a long, slow breath.

cards.question: After everything Josiah did, the LORD turns away from His burning anger against Judah.
The LORD's anger burns against Judah because of all that ___, a king of Judah before Josiah, had done to provoke Him.

cards.text: And this doesn't come out of nowhere. The writer tells us the LORD had already said what He would do.

cards.question: What had the LORD said He would do with Judah?

answers.text: Remove Judah from His sight as He did Israel
Give Judah peace for a hundred more years
Make Jerusalem the ruler over all nations

cards.text: The writer says the rest of Josiah's acts are written in the Book of the Chronicles of the Kings of Judah. Then the story picks up: during Josiah's reign, Pharaoh Neco king of Egypt marches up to help the king of Assyria at the Euphrates River.

cards.question: Pharaoh Neco king of Egypt is marching up toward the Euphrates. What does King Josiah do?

answers.text: Sends him a gift of gold

cards.question: King Josiah comes home alive from his face-off with Pharaoh Neco.
Pharaoh Neco faced King Josiah and killed him at ___.

cards.text: Josiah's servants carry his body in a chariot from Megiddo to Jerusalem and bury him in his own tomb. Then the people of the land need a new king.

cards.question: Who do the people of the land anoint and make king in Josiah's place?

findings.problem: The card says Josiah just finished tearing down idol altars from the temple all the way to Bethel. That comes from the passage before (2 Kings 23:4-20), but the card cites only 2 Kings 23:21 and gives no reference for it.

rule.text: Facts from outside the passage are fine when they help, like who a new person is or who wrote a letter, with their reference.

findings.problem: This story card repeats the answer to card 4 (since the judges, through all the kings) and adds a joke. It doesn't move the passage forward. It's a recap of 2 Kings 23:22, which cards 3 and 4 already covered.

The card says there's still stuff 'hiding' around the land. 2 Kings 23:24 says the abominations 'were seen in the land of Judah and in Jerusalem.' Saying they were hidden goes against what the text says.

rule.text: Retelling: Papa Dorin can retell in his own words and fill in what the text clearly implies. Scene-setting details are fine. He never says anything the text shows is wrong.

findings.problem: The setup gives away card 2's true or false answer. The 'Nevertheless' line followed by the boss taking a long, slow breath tells the baker bad news is coming, so 'True' (the LORD turns away from His anger) is ruled out before the baker answers.

rule.text: A setup line can't rule out the wrong answers either.

findings.problem: The question says Manasseh was 'a king of Judah before Josiah.' That fact comes from outside the passage (2 Kings 21:1), but the card cites only 2 Kings 23:26 and gives no reference for it.

rule.text: Facts from outside the passage are fine when they help, like who a new person is or who wrote a letter, with their reference.

findings.problem: The cards just before this one say the LORD's burning anger against Judah won't turn away. After that, 'Give Judah peace for a hundred more years' and 'Make Jerusalem the ruler over all nations' aren't believable, so the right answer stands out.

rule.text: Wrong answers for what someone does or says only need to be believable.

findings.problem: No card tells or asks the second half of 2 Kings 23:27: the LORD will reject Jerusalem, the city He chose, and the temple where He said His Name would be. This is a key detail of the passage, and the baker never sees it.

rule.text: When the baker leaves Prep, they understand the whole passage without missing an important detail.
